channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [Politico Europe] L’UE accusée de dissimuler l’impact environnemental des datacenters
item.description: Une ONG a déposé une plainte, affirmant que la Commission européenne dissimulerait des données sur la consommation d'énergie et d'eau des centres de données, portant ainsi atteinte au droit de savoir des citoyens.

item.title: [Financial Times] How will Trump ‘accord’ for AI to ‘self-regulate’ work?
item.description: US president touts voluntary commitment which may create unexpected legal liabilities for AI companies

item.title: [Politico Europe] ‘No way they can beat us’: Rutte rebuffs Russian nuclear threats to NATO
item.description: Moscow and NATO have exchanged tense letters in recent days following Russian opposition to alliance exercises near its Kaliningrad exclave.

item.title: [EU Observer] Where Russian maps place the occupiers, and where they really are — an overview of parts of the front (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,679)
item.description: Ukraine is losing the battle in the skies but holding strong on the battleground. And Russian media highlight “liberated” villages, but in reality they are still under Ukrainian control.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Y’a-t-il le feu au lac chez Edouard Philippe ?
item.description: Sans dynamique dans les sondages, Edouard Philippe parviendra-t-il à donner du souffle à sa campagne ? Le candidat Horizons a enfin présenté sa réforme des retraites qui prévoit de repousser l’âge légal de départ à 65 ans. Cela lui permettra-t-elle d’enlever le sparadrap du “candidat des 67 ans”, tout en convaincant les électeurs de droite […]

item.title: [EU Observer] US civil society groups call on EU not to delay methane rules
item.description: As Brussels moves to delay its methane rules, nearly 100 US civil society groups are urging EU governments not to cave to oil and gas lobbyists and the White House.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Macron and Sanchez say UK would be ‘welcome’ back in EU
item.description: Andy Burnham's suggestion that the U.K. could rejoin the EU was met with a more muted response from Brussels itself.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Europe’s energy security has a Black Sea opportunity
item.description: A second Libyan crude delivery and plans to expand the Kulevi Oil Refinery show how Black Sea Petroleum could broaden Europe’s fuel supply options.

item.title: [EU Observer] Let’s not allow AI firms to use fears of future dystopias to distract Europeans from existing problems
item.description: As Big Tech companies dramatise rogue AI and China fears, the real fight is over who pays the price for today’s fraud, failures and job threats — and who pockets the productivity gains.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Farage spoils for a Brexit brawl with Burnham
item.description: Reform UK leader will attack the prime minister’s turn towards Europe in a major speech Thursday.

item.title: [Financial Times] Netanyahu says pilot of Israel-bound flight tried to crash the plane
item.description: Plane carrying more than 150 passengers en route to Tel Aviv was diverted to Saudi Arabia after issuing ‘unlawful interference’ code

item.title: [Politico Europe] Eurozone inflation heats up faster than expected
item.description: Major eurozone economies see price growth above forecasts and at multi-year highs.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Das Anti-Euro-Dilemma
item.description: Die AfD steckt in einem Konflikt über ihre einstige Kernforderung. Während Parteichefin Alice Weidel und der europapolitische Sprecher Peter Boehringer den EU-Austritt als Ultima Ratio ins Spiel bringen, wirbt der Chef der Parteijugend Pascal Hohm für den Erhalt des Euro. Warum dieser Vorstoß für Turbulenzen sorgt, analysieren Pauline von Pezold und Frederik Schindler. In Sachsen-Anhalt […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU and Canada to announce sweeping new partnership pact
item.description: From critical raw materials to fighting wildfires, a document obtained by POLITICO reveals a wide-ranging expansion in relations.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Romanian political crisis deepens as parliament rejects PM nominee
item.description: A snap election is now possible but centrist President Nicușor Dan does not want a vote that would risk handing power to the far right.

item.title: [DW] Bosnia elections: Polls overshadowed by exhaustion, exodus and geopolitics as ethnic politics eclipse real problems
item.description: Bosnia goes to the polls on October 4 to elect several parliaments and presidents. While voters worry about the economy and emigration, the campaign is focused on ethnicity, exposing the country's political paralysis.

item.title: [Financial Times] Burnham says rejoining EU an option for UK
item.description: Prime minister says ‘going all the way’ is a possibility as government reviews relations with 27-country bloc

item.title: [EU Observer] Israeli outpost-linked firms exploit loophole to buy up European property even as the EU curbs trade with illegal settlements
item.description: From a €4m holiday resort in rural Finland to demolished Bedouin villages in the Negev, the same Israeli developer exposes how Europe’s new trade curbs on settlements still leave the door wide open for settlement-linked firms to profit on EU soil.

item.title: [Financial Times] Russia makes extreme threats against Nato countries over Kaliningrad
item.description: Kremlin accuses western defence alliance of preparing to blockade Russian exclave on Baltic Sea

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Ceuta crisis shows how EU border outsourcing puts children at risk, says German lawyer
item.description: By outsourcing border control to Morocco, Turkey or Albania and then panicking when they “open the gates,” German lawyer Lena Riemer says EU capitals have handed hostile regimes a cheap, reliable way to divide and humiliate Europe.

item.title: [Financial Times] At least Burnham doesn’t pretend to care about growth
item.description: Unlike his predecessors, Britain’s prime minister is a fairly honest stagnation-ist

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] 70% of Montenegro supports EU membership – so will it happen in 2028? We ask lead MEP Marjan Šarec
item.description: EUobserver spoke to Marjan Šarec, former Slovenian prime minister, MEP for Renew Europe, and the parliament’s rapporteur for Montenegro. He's keeping his optimism for the country’s accession.

item.title: [DW] Eurovision remains marred by geopolitics: Ireland will boycott again because of Israel's participation. Still, the song contest is expanding
item.description: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest was marred by boycotts in protest against Israel's participation in the midst of its war on Gaza. It still aims to keep growing.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Did the Spanish government address the protesters’ demands on housing?
item.description: The Spanish government strengthens tenants' rights amidst pressure from hundreds of protesters in Madrid.

item.title: [EU Observer] Divided EU cyber defence faces real-life Russian and Chinese threats
item.description: From phishing attacks on Polish soldiers to near-blackouts in winter, the EU’s fragmented cyber defence is seeing Russian online threats spill into real‑world dangers for ordinary Europeans.

item.title: [Financial Times] Ken Griffin donates record $3bn to Carnegie Mellon in push for Miami campus
item.description: Record contribution comes as the billionaire seeks to reshape the Florida city to rival the likes of New York and London

item.title: [DW] Hungary's reckoning with Orban's corrupt system picks up speed with high-profile arrests
item.description: Hungary's Prime Minister Peter Magyar vowed to dismantle Orban's corrupt networks. High-profile figures are being arrested and many Hungarians are pushing for swift accountability, but the rule of law takes time.

item.title: [Financial Times] AI industry moves to thwart data centre backlash ahead of US midterms
item.description: AI Infrastructure Coalition, whose members include Google, Meta and Microsoft, unveils commitments to cover energy costs and minimise water usage

item.title: [Financial Times] Is the world really drowning in debt?
item.description: We may not be on the eve of disaster but room for manoeuvre is shrinking for major economies

item.title: [Financial Times] How Nike fell off the pace in China
item.description: World’s biggest sports brand is tailoring its ranges for local tastes to get back on top in a market it pioneered

item.title: [Financial Times] Luxury watches must win back wrist space
item.description: The rise of health-tracking rings creates an opportunity for Cartier, Rolex and the like

item.title: [EU Observer] EU states urged to ‘go beyond’ AI Act to protect people from abusive surveillance
item.description: Peaceful protesters and ethnic minorities in Europe could be victimised by police abuse of AI-powered surveillance tech, an EU rights body has warned.

item.title: [EU Observer] Frugal EU states seeking budget cuts are shooting their own regions in the foot
item.description: Despite joining a frugal ultimatum for EU budget cuts, the Dutch get roughly as much growth from EU investment as they pay in, while narrowing the gap between wealthier and poorer regions.

item.title: [EU Observer] Former MEP Rachida Dati’s 2014 emails derided corruption allegations, which now form core of French trial
item.description: Former French MEP and culture minister Rachida Dati, who is now a Paris mayor, threatened to sue EUobserver in 2014 emails about corruption allegations, which are now coming home to roost in high-profile French trails.

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs vote for €47bn in new Erasmus+ funds, as frugal states seek cuts to EU budget
item.description: With 24 votes in favour and one abstention, MEPs proposed to increase the European Commission's original proposal from €40bn to €47bn on Tuesday.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU’s centre-right EPP seeks asylum opt-outs, as commission silent on new crisis rules
item.description: Political pressure for allowing EU asylum opt-outs continues to increase, as commission drafts vague new emergency rules in the wake of this summer's Ceuta episode.

item.title: [EU Observer] Scientists flee burning building in Kyiv’s mini-9/11, as Russian drone also explodes 200m from EU embassy (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,678)
item.description: Despite global audiences being numbed to daily Kyiv airstrikes and casualties, Russia's 9/11-type attack on a scientific institute, in a botched assassination attempt, still grabbed world attention.

item.title: [DW] UK PM Burnham seeks 'hope again' at Labour Party conference
item.description: Andy Burnham is seeking a delicate balance between optimism and realism at Labour's annual party conference. He promised hope and an end to "politics as usual" but also an "honest conversation" about difficult dilemmas.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU reduces funds for women’s rights groups, in wider budget bonfire of good causes
item.description: As the EU seeks budget cuts to break a stalemate in member states' talks, women's rights groups are on the chopping bloc, prompting advocates' concern that important causes are fading from the common agenda.

item.title: [DW] Albania: As corruption cases multiply, experts question whether the anti-corruption drive is addressing the causes or just the symptoms.
item.description: From a former president to the ex-intelligence chief, Albania is prosecuting senior officials at a rate once thought impossible. But do more prosecutions mean less corruption or simply better enforcement?

item.title: [DW] UK: US government questions bail for Fairford base suspects
item.description: The US government sees "the hand of a foreign actor" in the security scare at RAF Fairford, a hub for US heavy bombers in Europe. Donald Trump criticized the suspects being released on bail amid ongoing investigations.

item.title: [DW] European cities seek ways of boosting affordable housing
item.description: In many major urban centers of Europe, the housing shortage has become an explosive social issue. DW looks into various models that have been put in place across the continent.

item.title: [DW] Backlash over data centers tests Europe's AI ambitions
item.description: Massive data centers needed to run AI are triggering protests across Europe. Their operators counter that they boost digital sovereignty and energy independence.

item.title: [DW] Russia expected to intensify hybrid war on Europe
item.description: Drone explosions, airspace violations, arson attacks: Poland, Romania, and Moldova are now regularly targeted in Russian attacks against Ukraine. More governments are calling these attacks deliberate acts of aggression.

item.title: [DW] Russian classroom propaganda glorifies dying for your country, students say
item.description: The Russian government has stepped up its efforts to spread patriotic propaganda in schools. DW spoke to students about textbooks that portray the West as hostile and promote sacrifice for the nation.

item.title: [DW] Sicily: Mount Etna ash disrupts Catania flights again
item.description: A thick ash cloud from Mount Etna has been disrupting flights to Catania in Sicily for several days. Italy and Europe's most active volcano, Etna has impacted air travel several times this summer.

item.title: [DW] Turkey: Comedian convicted for 'insulting' Erdogan in show
item.description: Deniz Goktas was convicted of two of three charges, including "insulting" the president, but was released pending the appeal process. Nominally, Turkey is a secular country with free speech.

item.title: [DW] 'Lithuanian skies are NATO skies': DW speaks with Lithuanian premier Mindaugas Sinkevicius
item.description: In a DW interview, Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius discussed threats to Lithuania from Russia and Belarus, NATO's need for stronger air defense and why military spending alone cannot ensure security.

item.title: [DW] How Bulgaria become a global leader in battery storage and what this means for the country's grid and energy market?
item.description: In under two years, Bulgaria has become one of the world's most battery-intensive energy markets. Can the surge last — and what will it mean for conventional power generators?

item.title: [DW] Italy to ban burqa in schools, limit foreign pupils
item.description: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s government has passed new school rules capping the number of students who don't speak fluent Italian and banning face coverings.
